To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
valsartan reverses the post‐translinal modifications (PTMs) of the mitochondrial ATP synthase δ‐subunit during canine reperfused infarction.

the angiotensinal II type 1‐receptor blocker valsartan reverses the post‐translatory modifications (nitrosylation, oxidation, hydroxylation) of the δ‐ subunit of ATP synthases during in vivo canine myocardial reperfusion.
valsartan reverses PTMs of the ATP/δ during RMI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the mitochondrial metabolic protein ATP synthase δ‐subunit during ischemia‐reperfusion injury in the heart.
the identification and characterization of PTM of ATP/δ during canine RMI, and the potential of valsartan to reverse these changes.
the identification of the δ‐ subunit of ATP synthases (ATP/ δ) as a novel target for AT1R blockers in RMI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AT1R‐mediated cardioprotection by valsartan during RMI is related to inhibition of nitric oxidemediated chemical modifications and phosphorylation of ATP synthase.
valsartan reverses the post‐translitional modifications of the δ subunit of ATP synthases during in vivo canine RMI.
valsartan reversed post‐translative modifications of ATP synthase‐delta during in vivo canine RMI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AT1R‐inhibition by valsartan attenuates RMI‐induced cardiac dysfunction by inhibiting the nitric oxide pathway, which is associated with a reduction in the PTM of the ATP/δ subunit.
the AT1R blocker valsartan reverses PTM of the mitochondrial metabolic protein ATP/δ during RMI in dogs, which is associated with cardioprotection.
valsartan reversed PTMs of ATP/δ during reperfusion injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AT1R‐induced PTMs of ATP/δ are a novel mechanism for RMI cardioprotection.
AT1R blockade reverses the PTMs of ATP/δ during RMI, which might be a potential therapeutic target for RMI.

AT1R blockade can reverse the post‐translatory modifications of the mitochondrial ATP synthase δ‐subunit during in vivo canine myocardial infarctions, suggesting a potentially novel therapeutic approach for the prevention of cardiac dysfunction and remodeling.
